title: Get started with fieldopt
text: frame data frame one row per sampling unit (segment, farm, census block) coordinates. One row depot, office teams leave return . frame synthetic: forty segments 10 x 10 km square, crop area trends west east.

title: Get started with fieldopt
text: travel_matrix() computes matrix travel distances units. longitude latitude uses great-circle distances kilometres; planar coordinates, , Euclidean distances. matrix computed road network (example OSRM) can passed matrix argument better input exists. field_cost_model() turns routing solution money: cost per unit travel, fixed cost per visited unit (access, setting ) cost per interview.
code: m <- travel_matrix(frame, method = "euclidean") m #> Travel matrix: 41 units, euclidean (distance); mean off-diagonal 4.886. model <- field_cost_model(per_travel = 2, per_unit = 30, per_interview = 10,                           interviews_per_unit = 4, currency = "BRL") model #> Field cost model (BRL): 2 per travel unit, 30 per visited unit, 10 per #> interview.

title: Get started with fieldopt
text: select_units() draws spatially balanced probability sample local pivotal method: inclusion probabilities known, units close rarely selected together. Spatial balance usually lowers variance totals spatially structured variables; also spreads units territory, exactly makes field work longer. Making tension explicit point package. route_fieldwork() routes field work depot selected units. Without limits returns one tour; maximum length maximum number stops per route, splits work routes, one per team per day. solver GRASP heuristic local search optimal split tour, reports gap lower bound quality solution visible.  design_variance() gives Horvitz-Thompson estimate total crop variance local-mean estimator Grafström Schelin (2014), suits spatially balanced samples needs joint inclusion probabilities. variance sample size give simple random sampling shown comparison.
code: units <- frame[frame$unit != "depot", ] s <- select_units(units, n = 12) s[s$sampled, c("unit", "x", "y", "pi")] #> # A tibble: 12 × 4 #>    unit       x     y    pi #>    <chr>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #>  1 s7    4.66   9.29    0.3 #>  2 s8    8.61   2.95    0.3 #>  3 s18   0.0120 0.459   0.3 #>  4 s21   3.42   2.98    0.3 #>  5 s23   2.33   5.66    0.3 #>  6 s26   1.86   0.830   0.3 #>  7 s27   4.11   6.30    0.3 #>  8 s29   0.0543 5.72    0.3 #>  9 s30   6.02   6.62    0.3 #> 10 s31   9.11   8.78    0.3 #> 11 s34   0.162  8.58    0.3 #> 12 s40   4.47   9.00    0.3 r <- route_fieldwork(m, units = s$unit[s$sampled], depot = "depot",                      max_stops = 5, cost_model = model) r #>  #> ── Field routes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> 3 routes from "depot" through 12 units: total travel 47.06 distance (lower #> bound 32.89, gap 43.1%). #> Route 1 (19.58): s30 > s40 > s7 > s31 > s8 #> Route 2 (21.24): s21 > s26 > s18 > s29 > s34 #> Route 3 (6.229): s23 > s27 #> Cost (BRL): travel 94.11 + units 360 + interviews 480 = 934.1. autoplot(r) design_variance(s, y = "crop") #> # A tibble: 1 × 7 #>   total variance    se     cv variance_srs     n     N #>   <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>        <dbl> <int> <int> #> 1 1225.    4278.  65.4 0.0534        9568.    12    40 sum(frame$crop, na.rm = TRUE) #> [1] 1241.481

title: Get started with fieldopt
text: design chosen sample size, routing limits cost model. cost_variance_frontier() repeats select-route-price-estimate cycle grid sample sizes returns mean cost mean variance size: frontier survey planner faces.  frontier makes two questions answerable numbers: much next unit precision costs field, much different field organisation (teams, longer days, closer depot) change price. vignettes routing-teams frames--allocation take questions .
code: f <- cost_variance_frontier(frame, depot = "depot", cost_model = model,                             n_grid = c(6, 9, 12, 16, 20, 24), y = "crop",                             method = "euclidean", max_stops = 5,                             n_rep = 8, iterations = 60) f #> # A tibble: 6 × 8 #>       n cost_mean cost_sd travel_mean routes_mean variance_mean cv_mean n_rep #> * <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>       <dbl>       <dbl>         <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> #> 1     6      470.    5.81        24.9        2           17267.  0.102      8 #> 2     9      700.    5.18        34.8        2.12         6412.  0.0623     8 #> 3    12      924.    6.09        41.9        3            3449.  0.0467     8 #> 4    16     1221.    6.18        50.7        4            1494.  0.0311     8 #> 5    20     1517.    1.84        58.6        4.25          946.  0.0249     8 #> 6    24     1810.    3.33        65.1        5.5           519.  0.0184     8 autoplot(f)

title: Frames, strata and cost-aware allocation
text: cost column planning value per unit. area frame include travel, routing part package estimates: run cost_variance_frontier() area frame cost model, read mean cost per unit sample size consideration, use stratum cost. allocation reflects expensive segments really visit, loop can iterated twice stratum costs sample sizes agree. Overlap frames (farms present ) modelled ; allocation treats frames strata single design.
code: f <- cost_variance_frontier(area_frame, depot = "depot", cost_model = model,                             n_grid = c(40, 60, 80, 100), y = "crop") per_unit <- f$cost_mean / f$n strata$cost[strata$stratum == "area"] <- per_unit[which.min(abs(f$n - a$n[3]))] frame_allocation(strata, target_variance = 2.5e7)

title: Routing for one or several teams
code: one <- route_fieldwork(m, units = sel, depot = "depot", cost_model = model) one #>  #> ── Field routes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> 1 route from "depot" through 18 units: total travel 272 km (lower bound 230, #> gap 18.3%). #> Route 1 (272): s2 > s7 > s57 > s14 > s47 > s60 > s35 > s54 > s55 > s49 > s19 > #> s41 > s1 > s53 > s26 > s34 > s11 > s17 #> Cost (BRL): travel 489.7 + units 720 + interviews 1296 = 2506.

title: Routing for one or several teams
text: team must return depot every day maximum route length, 100 km. solver splits tour optimally limit (Prins 2004) improves route locally.
code: days <- route_fieldwork(m, units = sel, depot = "depot", max_length = 100,                         cost_model = model) days #>  #> ── Field routes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> 4 routes from "depot" through 18 units: total travel 345.3 km (lower bound 230, #> gap 50.2%). #> Route 1 (90.66): s17 > s53 > s1 > s41 #> Route 2 (83.6): s34 > s26 > s11 > s7 #> Route 3 (94.05): s2 > s57 > s14 > s47 > s60 > s35 #> Route 4 (77.03): s54 > s49 > s19 > s55 #> Cost (BRL): travel 621.6 + units 720 + interviews 1296 = 2638. autoplot(days)

title: Routing for one or several teams
text: team can interview four units day stop limit instead.
code: stops <- route_fieldwork(m, units = sel, depot = "depot", max_stops = 4,                          cost_model = model) stops #>  #> ── Field routes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> 5 routes from "depot" through 18 units: total travel 383.4 km (lower bound 230, #> gap 66.7%). #> Route 1 (90.66): s17 > s53 > s1 > s41 #> Route 2 (83.6): s34 > s26 > s11 > s7 #> Route 3 (39.02): s2 > s57 #> Route 4 (93.14): s14 > s47 > s60 > s35 #> Route 5 (77.03): s54 > s49 > s19 > s55 #> Cost (BRL): travel 690.2 + units 720 + interviews 1296 = 2706.

title: Routing for one or several teams
text: travel grows number routes every route starts ends depot; question planner whether extra kilometres cheaper extra days teams, cost model question, routing one.
code: data.frame(organisation = c("one tour", "100 km per route", "4 stops per route"),            routes = c(one$n_routes, days$n_routes, stops$n_routes),            travel_km = round(c(one$total, days$total, stops$total), 1),            cost = round(c(one$cost[["total"]], days$cost[["total"]], stops$cost[["total"]]))) #>        organisation routes travel_km cost #> 1          one tour      1     272.0 2506 #> 2  100 km per route      4     345.3 2638 #> 3 4 stops per route      5     383.4 2706

text: Distances coordinates understate travel real roads. routing engine available, pass matrix: units must order coordinates, used names plots.

text: iterations number GRASP restarts; alpha greediness construction (0 pure greedy, 1 pure random). default 200 iterations alpha = 0.3 enough hundred units; gap field reports far solution two-edge lower bound, loose, gaps 20 40 percent normal good solutions.

title: Field-Survey Design under Real Field Cost
text: Field-survey design real field cost. Survey samples usually designed precision alone; cost actually decides whether survey happens field work: travelling sampling units interviewing. fieldopt puts cost next variance estimator visible design chosen. travel_matrix() builds travel matrix units coordinates (great-circle planar distances) wraps road-network matrix. field_cost_model() turns travel, visits interviews money time. route_fieldwork() routes field work depot selected units, one team several, route-length stop limits (GRASP 2-opt, -opt optimal split tour), reports gap lower bound. select_units() draws spatially balanced probability sample local pivotal method, equal size-proportional inclusion probabilities. design_variance() gives Horvitz-Thompson total local-mean variance estimate, simple-random-sampling variance reference. frame_allocation() allocates sample across strata frames target variance minimum cost, budget minimum variance. cost_variance_frontier() simulates designs grid sample sizes returns trade-field cost variance. numerical engine Rust crate fieldopt-core, usable Rust languages.

title: Field-Survey Design under Real Field Cost
text: development version needs Rust toolchain (cargo rustc 1.70 later, https://rustup.rs):
code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("castlaboratory/fieldopt")

title: Field-Survey Design under Real Field Cost
code: library(fieldopt)  set.seed(1) frame <- data.frame(unit = c("depot", paste0("s", 1:40)),                     x = c(5, runif(40, 0, 10)), y = c(5, runif(40, 0, 10))) frame$crop <- c(NA, 20 + 3 * frame$x[-1] + rnorm(40))  model <- field_cost_model(per_travel = 2, per_unit = 30, per_interview = 10,                           interviews_per_unit = 4, currency = "BRL")  # one design: select, route, price, estimate units <- frame[frame$unit != "depot", ] s <- select_units(units, n = 12) m <- travel_matrix(frame, method = "euclidean") r <- route_fieldwork(m, units = s$unit[s$sampled], depot = "depot",                      max_stops = 5, cost_model = model) r design_variance(s, y = "crop")  # the frontier across sample sizes f <- cost_variance_frontier(frame, depot = "depot", cost_model = model,                             n_grid = c(8, 12, 16, 24), y = "crop",                             method = "euclidean", max_stops = 5, n_rep = 10) autoplot(f)
